templates.description: Historical structural pressure transmission linking fiscal/subsistence stress to elite bargaining breakdowns and mobilization.
Coordinated mass mobilization threatens regime continuity only once leadership factions fracture or security-apparatus loyalty wavers.
Concentrated decision-making and the loss of public accountability erode long-run institutional legitimacy.
Persistent seasonal flooding reduces market access and household trade in isolated settlements.
Multi-front expansion stretches industrial resource base, fuel stockpiles, and garrison manpower faster than occupied territory yields extractable surplus.
